digest.component_or_area: codebase refactoring and duplication elimination across multiple subsystems
propositions: Defect review identified duplicated decision logic appearing 2–7 times across the codebase, causing fixes to land in only one copy while twins remain broken and arrive as multi-ticket families

Consolidation children must collapse each duplicated computation into exactly one shared module while preserving all pinned observable behaviour and producing net-negative non-test line counts across the set

Each consolidation child must include a construct-uniqueness guard test that asserts exactly one implementation exists, using distinctive atoms or AST shape matching rather than single common tokens, with mandatory escape markers and reasons

Acceptance criteria AC2 and AC3 empirically fail as written: AC2's tests-only-additions proxy is violated by consolidations legitimately deleting duplicate test copies and re-pointing references; AC3's net-negative-lines criterion measured +2449 net lines across 23 children and is unachievable without stripping required documentation

The epic encompasses thirteen consolidation children (StorePaths, stamped lock, cascade, replacement walk, token twins, fit_for_send, nested pytest, gate policy, and five unnamed) plus nine hardening children with separate acceptance criteria

Plan-review and code-review gates require that the consolidation must include rationale docstrings explaining why a computation was extracted, making the net-negative-lines metric incompatible with those quality signals
